title: Multiscale signed contact-chain conditioning
coverage_gap: The exact N10 support has five LL and five HH layouts; it lacks the LH/HL peg_y versus box_y recombinations and all specified extrapolation ranges. A policy using absolute peg_y as a proxy for box_y can fit this support without learning the correct independent grasp and insertion errors.
reusable_regularity: Represent the manipulation as signed world-frame hand-to-pegGrasp and pegHead-to-goal edges. Both metric and smooth fine-scale coordinates are supplied; the fine features improve resolution near contact without erasing long distances. There is no hard stage switch or scripted action. A shared DP learns motion from these 48 features per observation. The observed approximately 0.13 m head/grasp separation makes those two sites noninterchangeable. Fixed metric scales avoid dividing nearly constant quaternion or goal-height channels by tiny fitted standard deviations.
dependencies_preserved: hand, pegGrasp, pegHead and goal remain distinct; the head-to-grasp vector preserves rigid shape and possible orientation changes
world axes and separate absolute hand/world coordinates are retained; relative edges plus hand recover all current positions, including the goal identifying the fixed-orientation box
world z heights of hand, grasp, head and goal preserve gravity, tabletop clearance and elevated hole geometry
current and previous object orientation are represented by two rotation columns and their difference; equivalent quaternion signs give identical rotations
native current-versus-previous hand/peg step displacements, gripper aperture/change and both whole causal observations retain contact and motion dependencies
goal-to-hand and insertion transverse distances expose the box relation; no collision-free-path or unseen obstacle information is assumed

expected_failure_signature: If relative coordinates alone are insufficient, failures should concentrate at lift/transport transitions and at small transverse insertion errors, rather than simple initial reaching. Large opposite-sign peg/box offsets may cause premature lateral transport while the peg is low because no explicit stage or collision model is imposed. The model can still exploit absolute hand/world correlations, so extrapolation is not guaranteed. These are pre-feedback predictions, not measured outcomes.

required_runtime_fields.omitted: Only the declared absent object2 zero blocks are discarded. No reset factors, time index, success signal, future observation or simulator state is read.
required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity encode/decode: [world_dx, world_dy, world_dz, gripper]. Translation units remain native 0.01 m per action unit; gripper is unchanged. Only the executor clips native actions, and it executes the common first four of sixteen predictions.

support_fit: None. Constants are physical representation scales, not learned statistics. The host's D_N normalizer is unchanged; this representation uses raw causal observations for metric differences.
change_summary: Initial pre-feedback design. Replaces raw normalized conditioning with a deterministic 48-dimensional contact-chain representation; no added learned modules, extra losses, action mappings, or changes to the shared DP/training budget.
